correctness.rationale: Exact quadratic-residue character sum normalized by m=(p-1)/2 yields E offdiagonal -1+i√p χ(b-a). Four symbolic canonical tournament determinants give P_T,P_D,P_S. Doubly regular Paley out-neighborhoods yield N_T,N_D and N_S from ordered source and sink counting. Sharp root-sign identities show T uniquely dominates S and D for p≥11, and S dominates D at p7, and simple-root scaling gives δ4~(1+√2)/√p. Symbolic checker confirms polynomial identities and direct Fourier enumerations for all 13,096 four-subsets at p=7,11,19,23 corroborate, without replacing the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Renes already provides the general tournament Gram formula, while the exact four-subset characteristic-polynomial census, multiplicities and strict global δ4 optimization require additional determinant, regular-neighborhood counting and root-comparison arguments. Satake treats the RIP of a different augmented Paley matrix and conditional high-order bounds, not this complete small-order complex unaugmented calculation. Magsino–Mixon–Parshall addresses asymptotic random real-Paley subensembles. Published-record published-finding corpus searches returned adjacent but noncovering four-point Fourier/phase results. Residual priority risk of older four-vertex tournament spectral results remains; no independent originality certification.

value.rationale: Sharp four-sparse restricted isometry/spectral deviation of a canonical deterministic harmonic frame is a natural quantitative stability invariant. The theorem classifies all four-column eigenvalue multisets, counts exactly how often each occurs, and characterizes all sharp equality cases, including a nontrivial exceptional prime. These results are not just a coherence bound or renaming of the known ETF Gram representation.
